income_group_note: Table 6 (advanced, 0.223-0.367) and Table 7 (less advanced, 0.031-0.265, none significant) match. Only a two-way split at USD 10,000 5-year average GDP per capita is used, defined on contemporaneous income; Table 2 groups (91 + 165 = 256) exceed 217 economies because countries switch groups across periods. Record's note that World Bank groups are not used is right.

risk_of_bias.why: Overall serious is defensible because patents measure invention not AI use and causal wording ('AI-related innovation drives long-run economic growth') outruns the design. The confounding domain is a little harsh: the paper does address reverse causality (internal-lag GMM, FE-IV with cited non-patent literature, Sargan-Hansen and endogeneity tests), so moderate is closer, though exclusion is doubtful and lags were tuned to pass tests (footnote 42). Record's 'close to n=122' for 65 instruments is overstated (it is close for the advanced sample, 42 vs 53, footnote 47); the real excess is Table 9 GMM with 121 instruments for n=120. Exposure: serious fits (text search patents, footnotes 8, 30, 46). Selective reporting: all estimators and insignificant results are shown; moderate is acceptable.

problems: No invented numbers or mixed-up papers found; all quoted coefficients, SEs, N and n match Tables 3-9 and the 'Table 10 AI GMM 0.769**' claim matches. Issues: (1) heterogeneity 1 understates where the advanced x AI interaction is significant (Table 8 FE, Table 9, Table 10); (2) '65 instruments close to n=122' overstated, while Table 9 GMM (121 instruments, n=120) is the real proliferation problem; (3) result 7 is a non-AI comparator; (4) sample_corrections none needed (122 / 217 / 144 economies, 1970-2019 confirmed). Table 10 is only referenced in footnote 41, so 'not discussed' is correct.
